name: H200 NVL
notes: Unlike H100 NVL (a factory-bonded fixed 2-card pair using three NVLink bridges for 600 GB/s), H200 NVL ships as an INDIVIDUAL PCIe card supporting a single wide NVLink bridge, field-installable in either a 2-slot (spans 2 cards, 900 GB/s total bridge bandwidth) or 4-slot (spans 4 cards, 1800 GB/s total) configuration -- per the official H200 NVL Product Brief (PB-12128-001_v01). nvlink_bridge_gpu_count/nvlink_max_domain_size record the maximum supported group size (4); nvlink_bandwidth_gbps records the stated per-GPU bidirectional figure (900 GB/s) which is the datasheet's headline number regardless of bridge size chosen. tdp_watts_max of 600W is both default and max per the product brief's power table (600W default/max, 350W compliance limit, 200W minimum) -- more configurable-down than fixed. Per the H200 datasheet's footnote convention, TF32/BF16/FP16/FP8/INT8 Tensor Core figures are sparse-only, no independently published dense value. FP6 Tensor Core not applicable (Hopper predates FP6, introduced in Blackwell). cuda_cores/tensor_cores/sm_count left null -- not published by NVIDIA for H200 in any form factor (see h200-sxm-141gb.json notes for detail). process_node_nm of 4 (TSMC 4N) IS directly sourced for H200 -- NVIDIA's Hopper architecture page names H200 by product name in the same sentence as the TSMC 4N claim, a stronger citation than the H200 product datasheet itself (see h200-sxm-141gb.json notes for the exact quote). release_date of 2023-11-13 is NVIDIA's official H200 announcement at SC23 (same event covers both SXM and NVL form factors). Memory bandwidth stated as '4.8TB/s' in the datasheet; the NVL product brief gives a more precise 4,813 GB/s for the same figure -- consistent, not a discrepancy.

_sources.nvlink_bridge_gpu_count: H200 NVL Product Brief (PB-12128-001_v01), Ch.1 Overview: 'the NVIDIA H200 NVL uses a single wide NVLink bridge per card... allows up to four NVIDIA H200 NVL PCIe cards to be connected'
_sources.nvlink_bandwidth_gbps: H200 NVL Product Brief (PB-12128-001_v01), Table 4-2: 2-slot bridge = 900 GB/s total; 4-slot bridge = 1,800 GB/s total
_sources.tdp_watts_max: H200 NVL Product Brief (PB-12128-001_v01), Table 2-1: 'PCIe 16-pin cable strapped for 600W power mode: 600W maximum (default), 350W power compliance limit, 200W minimum'
_sources.nvlink_generation: NVIDIA HGX H100 and HGX H200 Datasheet (doc 3361709, Jul'24): 'NVLink: Fourth generation'
_sources.process_node_nm: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/technologies/hopper-architecture/ ('Built with over 80 billion transistors using a cutting edge TSMC 4N process... fuel the NVIDIA H200 and H100 Tensor Core GPUs')
_sources.slot_width: H200 NVL Product Brief (PB-12128-001_v01): 'The NVIDIA H200 NVL card is a dual-slot 10.5-inch PCI Express Gen5 card'; 'Mechanical form factor: Full-height, full-length (FHFL) 10.5", dual-slot'. Distinct from the '2-slot or 4-slot NVLink bridge' terminology elsewhere in the same brief, which describes bridge span (see nvlink_bridge_gpu_count), not this card's own physical width.
